claim: The audited clean dataset contains 180 main-analysis trials linked through immutable record identities.
numerical_result: 186 audited records; 174 main_unique + 6 main_valid_replacement = 180 main trials; 6 known-error records excluded; 186/186 raw/events/summary triplets verified
statistical_evidence: Descriptive provenance audit; no inferential test
allowed_wording: The audited lineage yielded 180 main-analysis trials while retaining six known-error records outside the analysis.
forbidden_wording: The erroneous files were deleted or silently overwritten.
limitation: Record validity follows the documented 20260729/20260730 replacement decision.

claim: Participant is the independent human experimental unit.
statistical_evidence: All outcome contrasts use five paired participant means
figure_table: Fig. 3; Fig. 5; Table II; Table III
allowed_wording: Inference was conducted at the participant level (n=5).
forbidden_wording: The study included 180 independent human observations or 45 independent blocks.
limitation: Repeated trials improve within-participant estimation but not the number of independent humans.

claim: G adaptation was active before task start in most G trials.
supporting_data: First activation aligned to task start
numerical_result: 42/45 before task start; median offset -0.3790 s
allowed_wording: G adaptation began before task start in 42 of 45 trials.
forbidden_wording: G was activated only after task start.
limitation: Timing incidence characterizes implementation fidelity, not independent human-level efficacy.

claim: G adaptation was active before logged contact in most G trials.
numerical_result: 43/45 before contact; median offset -1.2144 s; 2/45 at or after contact
allowed_wording: G adaptation preceded logged contact in 43 of 45 trials.
forbidden_wording: G was a pure post-contact force-feedback condition.
limitation: Contact onset was detected from the logged threshold rather than an independent contact sensor.

claim: The G pre-activation pattern coincided with raw-force gating and activation before baseline readiness.
supporting_data: Raw force at first activation and baseline-relative timing
numerical_result: 45/45 first activations occurred above 1 N raw estimated force; 42/45 before baseline ready
statistical_evidence: Code/log consistency audit; not a randomized mechanism contrast
allowed_wording: The observed G timing was consistent with the raw-force threshold and initialization sequence.
forbidden_wording: The individual causal contribution of the deadband, baseline, or initialization was isolated.

claim: The intended 0.20-s F activation gate was not realized in most trials.
supporting_data: First F activation aligned to contact
statistical_evidence: Descriptive timing audit; audited code mixed time.time and perf_counter domains
allowed_wording: F first activated a median of 0.053 s after contact, with 42 of 45 activations earlier than the intended 0.20-s gate.
forbidden_wording: F correctly implemented a 0.20-s post-contact gate.
limitation: The three later activations coincided with late vision locking and do not validate the intended gate.

claim: Vision locking did not precede contact in every E or F trial.
supporting_data: Vision lock aligned to task start and contact
numerical_result: E: median +1.7408 s from task start and -0.7546 s from contact; 5/45 post-contact. F: +1.7520 s from task start and -0.9411 s from contact; 3/45 post-contact
allowed_wording: Vision lock generally preceded contact but occurred after contact in 5 E and 3 F trials.
forbidden_wording: Every E/F trial received its vision-based configuration before contact.
limitation: The clean data identify timing heterogeneity but do not isolate the visual mechanism.

claim: A/G/E/F are bundled realized logged configurations rather than a strict realized 2x2 factorial manipulation.
numerical_result: G pre-contact in 43/45; F earlier than intended gate in 42/45; post-contact vision lock in 5/45 E and 3/45 F trials
figure_table: Fig. 1; Fig. 2; Table I; Table IV
allowed_wording: The four modes were analyzed as realized logged bundled configurations.
forbidden_wording: The comparisons identify independent visual and force main effects or their interaction.
limitation: Other parameter bundling and incomplete order balance also constrain factorial interpretation.

claim: Participant-level mean threshold-referenced excess-force impulse differed descriptively across realized logged configurations.
statistical_evidence: Descriptive participant-level means; contrasts reported separately
allowed_wording: E and F had lower descriptive participant-level mean threshold-referenced impulse than A and G.
forbidden_wording: Trial counts prove population-level superiority of E/F.
limitation: Mode means do not isolate component mechanisms.

claim: Initial peak-force mode means showed a pattern concordant with the impulse means.
statistical_evidence: Descriptive participant-level means; E-A contrast reported separately
allowed_wording: The initial peak-force pattern was descriptively concordant with the impulse pattern.
forbidden_wording: All safety metrics were significantly improved by vision.
limitation: Initial peak force is a secondary outcome.

claim: All clean trials met the software-log success definition.
numerical_result: 180/180 trials; participant-level success 1.0 in every mode
statistical_evidence: No comparative inference because there was no observed variation
allowed_wording: All clean trials met the archived software-log success definition.
forbidden_wording: All physical task outcomes were independently verified.
limitation: Success was derived primarily from software event logs.

claim: E was associated with lower participant-mean threshold-referenced excess-force impulse than A.
statistical_evidence: t(4)=-3.7393, paired t p=0.0201; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted p: t=0.0633, sign-flip=0.2500, Wilcoxon=0.2500
allowed_wording: E was associated with lower threshold-referenced excess-force impulse than A, with consistent direction but limited confirmatory strength.
forbidden_wording: E significantly reduced force under all tests; vision or stiffness caused the reduction.
limitation: n=5; exploratory analysis; E is a bundled configuration.

claim: The observed E-A threshold-referenced impulse direction was consistent across participants and LOPO subsets.
numerical_result: 5/5 participant differences negative; LOPO estimates -0.4028 to -0.2860 N*s, all negative
statistical_evidence: One LOPO 95% t-CI crossed zero; LOPO is a stability diagnostic
allowed_wording: All five observed participant differences and all five LOPO estimates retained the same direction.
forbidden_wording: The contrast was significant in every LOPO analysis or confirmed in the population.
limitation: Each LOPO subset contains only four participants and has imprecise intervals.

claim: The E-A initial peak-force contrast was directionally concordant but not robust to multiplicity correction.
statistical_evidence: paired t p=0.0263; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted t p=0.0789 and exact/Wilcoxon p=0.2500
allowed_wording: Initial peak force showed a concordant directional E-A difference.
forbidden_wording: E significantly reduced initial peak force after correction.
limitation: Secondary outcome with the same n=5 and bundled-mode limitations.

claim: The lower E-A force estimate was accompanied by longer task-start-to-contact time.
statistical_evidence: t(4)=18.1647, paired t p=5.40e-05; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted p: t=0.000162, sign-flip=0.2500, Wilcoxon=0.2500
allowed_wording: E was accompanied by longer participant-mean task-start-to-contact time than A.
forbidden_wording: Vision caused operators to move more slowly, or the interval directly measured robot approach duration.
limitation: Task start marked system readiness; mode order, operator behavior, vision timing, and bundled controller differences cannot be separated.

claim: The lower E-A force estimate was accompanied by longer total task time.
statistical_evidence: t(4)=5.2723, paired t p=0.00620; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted p: t=0.0186, sign-flip=0.2500, Wilcoxon=0.2500
allowed_wording: The E-A pattern was consistent with a safety-efficiency trade-off.
forbidden_wording: A causal safety-efficiency mechanism or mediation effect was established.
limitation: The paired outcomes establish association, not mechanism.

claim: G showed a small average threshold-referenced impulse difference from A under the realized logged G implementation.
statistical_evidence: t(4)=-1.6672, paired t p=0.1708; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted t p=0.3416
allowed_wording: Under the realized logged G implementation, the G-A estimate was small and its interval included zero.
forbidden_wording: Pure post-contact force feedback reduced force.

claim: F showed no stable incremental threshold-referenced impulse advantage over E under the realized logged implementation.
supporting_data: Participant-level main metric and LOPO contrast
statistical_evidence: t(4)=-0.4810, paired t p=0.6556; exact sign-flip p=0.6875; Wilcoxon p=0.8125; LOPO changed sign after excluding P03
allowed_wording: No discernible incremental F-over-E advantage was observed under the realized logged implementation.
forbidden_wording: Force refinement was ineffective or F and E were equivalent.
limitation: F did not realize its intended 0.20-s gate and the interval allows effects in either direction.

claim: The F-G threshold-referenced impulse contrast is descriptive and does not identify visual-force synergy.
statistical_evidence: t(4)=-4.0232, paired t p=0.0158; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted t p=0.0633 and exact/Wilcoxon p=0.2500
allowed_wording: F and G differed descriptively under their realized logged implementations.
forbidden_wording: F significantly outperformed G because of visual-force synergy.
limitation: G and F contain different bundled and mistimed interventions.
